toscano--toscano-classico.description: Toscano Classico is machine-made by Manifatture Sigaro Toscano from fire-cured Kentucky tobacco: an Italian-grown wrapper, no binder, and a filler of Italian and American leaf, rested for about six months after rolling. Behind the smoky, pipe-like aroma it smokes nutty and gently sweet, with wood and earth, and sits well beside an espresso.

thirds.notes: Smooth and nutty, with a soft sweetness and a background note of coffee in a cool, creamy smoke.
The thicker middle of the cheroot adds a woodier tone to the nutty base.
Nuttiness returns with subtle earth to close.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Toscano Classico review
Italian Smokes – A primer on Toscano

toscano--toscano-antico.description: Toscano Antico is one of the brand's machine-made staples, rolled from fire-cured Kentucky tobacco that is fermented longer than the Classico's and aged around twelve months. The result is a stronger, full-bodied cheroot with a spicy, savoury character; cut in half, it becomes the Toscanello Speciale.

sources.title: Italian Smokes – A primer on Toscano

toscano--toscano-extra-vecchio.description: Extra Vecchio, 'extra old', is made from fire-cured Kentucky tobacco given a long fermentation and several years of ageing, then rested again after machine rolling. It is a dry, uncompromising cheroot of smoked wood, charcoal, dark chocolate, leather and earth with a long finish, for seasoned smokers and a glass of grappa.

sources.title: Italian Smokes – A primer on Toscano

toscano--toscano-garibaldi.description: Garibaldi belongs to Toscano's Sigari d'Autore series, recognisable by its green box, and draws on Kentucky tobacco grown in southern Italy, in Campania and Umbria, for part of its character. It is one of the lighter, mellower Toscano cheroots and a popular lighter choice in the range.

sources.title: Italian Smokes – A primer on Toscano

toscano--toscano-originale.description: Toscano Originale is rolled by hand by the sigaraie in Lucca, with American Kentucky in the wrapper and part of the coarsely chopped filler, blended with Italian leaf. It is a long, strong cheroot with bold, fire-cured flavour and a little sweetness underneath.

sources.title: Italian Smokes – A primer on Toscano

toscano--toscano-il-moro.description: Il Moro is hand-rolled in small yearly quantities: about 230 mm long and up to 20 mm thick, it is the only Toscano sold in its own wooden box. It is one of the strongest and most exclusive cigars in the range, kept for special occasions.

sources.title: Italian Smokes – A primer on Toscano

toscano--toscanello.description: Toscanello is the short Toscano: a Classico cut in half, mostly machine-made near Naples from Kentucky tobacco. Lighter than the full-length cheroots, it is a quick smoke, and the range also includes aromatic versions such as coffee, vanilla, chocolate and hazelnut.

sources.title: Italian Smokes – A primer on Toscano

toscano--toscano-master-aged.description: Master Aged is Toscano's handmade premium series, rolled in Lucca as a 6.3 by 40 double-tapered cheroot from roughly half Tuscan tobacco and half fire-cured American leaf. Each edition changes the wrapper or its treatment, and the first rests 360 days in cellars. Full-bodied, it moves from savoury opening notes to nuts and cream.

thirds.notes: The opening differs by edition, from toffee and leather to earthy, herbal tones, often with pepper or malt on the retrohale.
The editions converge on nuts, from macadamia to walnut and hazelnut, with a buttery, creamy feel and smoother smoke.
Smoky wood, hickory or cedar and charcoal close the smoke, often with a dark, fruity note.
